items.title: TASK-095 — The Avatar has hands — Hey Clicky parity: a real pointer that glides, clicks, and types, behind explicit control consent
items.outcome: The desktop Avatar does what Hey Clicky does: given a task, it looks at the consented screen, decides one action at a time, glides the REAL macOS pointer along a human-looking arc, clicks, types, presses allowlisted keys, scrolls, and opens apps, narrating each step, until the task is done, refused, stopped, or bounded — and its on-screen pointer is a proper arrow glyph that flies (the clicky flight arc) instead of a ring. Control is opt-in per request, Accessibility-gated, privacy-guarded every step, and the user's hand always wins: moving the mouse mid-glide halts the run.
items.prototypeTest: On a real desktop build with Screen Recording + Accessibility granted and a Groq key, open the companion panel → Do, turn on "Let Zazoo use my mouse and keyboard", type "open Notes and write hello" → the arrow glyph and the real cursor glide to the Notes icon/field, a click ring flashes, text is typed, the step list narrates each step with ✓, and the run ends "Done". Move the mouse during a glide → the run stops within a tick and says so. Turn the switch off → `act_start` refuses with `ACT_CONTROL_NOT_ALLOWED` and nothing moves. Revoke Accessibility → refuses with `ACT_NO_ACCESSIBILITY` and prompts. A password-manager window frontmost → the run halts before capture.
scope: `actuator.rs` (CGEvent move/click/type/key/scroll, smoothstep Bézier glide, takeover detection), `act.rs` (bounded look-decide-act loop, closed planner vocabulary, `act_start/act_poll/act_stop`), `AgentPointer.tsx` (arrow glyph + flight), `DoRun.tsx` + Do mode in `CompanionAsk.tsx`, `companion_capabilities.accessibility`, `monitor_logical_rect`.
